t: You're looking at a statue of Queen Victoria, put up in 2007, standing in Victoria Square in SW1. Victoria came to the throne in 1837 and reigned until 1901, longer than any monarch before her. Those sixty-three years gave us the Victorian era, a time of great industrial, political, scientific and military change, with the British Empire expanding enormously. In 1876, Parliament also voted her the extra title of Empress of India. So the figure here represents a queen whose name still marks this whole part of London.
